solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Theatre company dine and do it all over again

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre company
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors sit down to a meal and then go through the whole show a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something all over again is to perform it once more, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Starving bird needing nothing from America

parts.note: a raven is a large black bird
O looks like zero, nothing
US stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A hungry bird is not being fed by the Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing nothing' suggests a lack, but nothing simply supplies O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means extremely hungry, a strong synonym for starving.

clue.text: The sort of cats and dogs that rain down on fortifications?

parts.note: paras, paratroopers, rain down from the sky
cats and dogs are pets

explanation.surface: A play on the idiom of raining cats and dogs, with animals falling onto castle walls.
explanation.walkthrough: Pets that parachute would be 'para pets'; the question mark admits the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Parapets are protective low walls on ramparts, a type of defensive fortification.

clue.text: Warding off voting system can get between monarch and government

parts.note: AV is the alternative vote, an electoral system

indicators.note: get between puts one piece in the gap between two others

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A voting reform could intervene between Crown and government to stave off trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher, so a crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Averting means turning away or preventing, a synonym for warding off a danger.

clue.text: Jeez! That's that writer!

parts.note: Jeez is a softened form of the exclamation Christ!
that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise on recognising a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie, the detective novelist, is the writer; 'that writer' just points at her.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was a prolific author of detective fiction, so she is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Comedian finds lines in French on troubled life difficult to grasp

indicators.note: to grasp means the outer word holds the others within it

parts.note: hard means difficult
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines
en is French for in

indicators.note: troubled says the letters of life are disturbed

explanation.surface: A comedian finds French verse on a troubled life hard to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges LIFE into FIEL; HARD grasps RY, EN and FIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Enfield is a British comic actor known for sketch shows, an example of a comedian.

clue.text: Not guilty, hence trial collapses

indicators.note: collapses says the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A defendant is acquitted because the trial falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapses' rearranges HENCE TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cleared of suspicion or blame is free of guilt, an idiomatic phrase for innocent.

clue.text: Iggy Pop initially put his foot down about photographer's equipment

indicators.note: about means the stepping word goes around the letters

parts.note: trod means put a foot down

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: The rock singer Iggy Pop stamps his foot over camera gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put his foot down' looks like the idiom for being firm, but here it is read literally as stepping.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand holding a camera steady, a piece of photographic kit.

clue.text: Little bird begins eating the end of a shoelace

indicators.note: begins takes the first letter of eating

parts.note: an aglet is the plastic or metal tag at the end of a shoelace

explanation.surface: A baby bird starts pecking at the tip of a shoelace.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, so a little or baby bird.

clue.text: Luxurious fabric changes hands for a monkey

indicators.note: the left-hand letter is swapped for the right-hand one, since L and R stand for left and right

parts.note: velvet is a soft, rich fabric

explanation.surface: A piece of plush cloth is traded and ends up being swapped for a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes hands' turns the L (left) in VELVET into R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: A vervet is a small African monkey with a black face, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Herts town hosting excessive form of horse-racing

indicators.note: a town hosting something has it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire (Herts)
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A Hertfordshire town puts on an over-the-top race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the usual short form of Hertfordshire, an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotting is harness racing in which horses pull a light cart at a trot, one type of horse-racing.

clue.text: Uncontrollable delight sank a TV panel discussion

indicators.note: uncontrollable says the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild joy sinks a television debate show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncontrollable' rearranges DELIGHT SANK A.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking heads are pundits filmed from the shoulders up, the staple of a television studio discussion.

clue.text: Spick's returning partner snoozes

indicators.note: returning means the partner word is read from the back

parts.note: in the phrase spick and span, the word partnering spick is span

explanation.surface: Someone's other half comes home and promptly dozes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spick's partner' is SPAN from the phrase 'spick and span'; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Naps are short sleeps, and as a verb a person who naps snoozes: direct synonyms.

clue.text: Return English prize, possibly with unknown stuff, to the London area

indicators.note: Return tells us to read the whole string of pieces back to front

parts.note: a Nobel is one example of a prize
Y is a mathematical unknown
to stuff is to ram in

explanation.surface: Someone is told to send back an English award along with mysterious material to a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns ENOBELYRAM round as a whole to give the district.
explanation.definitionFit: Marylebone is a district of central London, so it is one London area.

clue.text: Tact shown by princess's making no announcement at first

parts.note: Di was Princess Diana; with the possessive, Di's

indicators.note: no says the letter is left out

parts.note: creation is a making of something

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of announcement

explanation.surface: A princess shows tact by not saying anything at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no announcement at first' removes the A from CREATION, giving CRETION.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is careful judgement in speech and behaviour, a close synonym for tact.

clue.text: Carelessly obese royal

parts.note: obese means not thin, which can be written un-thin
kingly means royal, befitting a king

explanation.surface: A rude remark about an overweight member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obese' is read as 'un-thin', a whimsical made-up word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without thinking means doing it heedlessly, so the adverb matches 'carelessly'.

clue.text: Competed with duke after John rose in anger

indicators.note: after puts the duke letter at the end
in puts the turned word inside the anger word

parts.note: to rile is to anger

indicators.note: rose in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, a lav

explanation.surface: A duke joined the contest once John got angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns LAV upwards to VAL; 'in' sets it in RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rivalled someone is to have competed with them as an equal.

clue.text: Financial backer apparently lost his shirt on gold

parts.note: someone without a shirt is apparently in vest, in an undershirt
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A backer seems to have lost everything betting on gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost his shirt' looks like the idiom for losing all one's money, but read literally a shirtless man is 'in vest'.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor puts money into a business, so is a financial backer.

clue.text: Northern European reportedly inspected home of birds

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the word rather than see its spelling

parts.note: scanned means inspected closely
in means at home
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A northern European is said to have checked over a bird sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives SCAND, which sounds like 'scanned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandinavians come from Norway, Sweden or Denmark, so one is a Northern European.

clue.text: TV doctor, losing his first children outside, faints

indicators.note: outside means the children word wraps around the shortened doctor

parts.note: sons are children

indicators.note: losing says a letter is taken away from the doctor

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time-travelling television doctor

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of his

explanation.surface: A television doctor faints when he loses his eldest children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his first' is the H that starts 'his', not the doctor's own first letter, though both happen to be H here.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, especially from emotion, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In shock, books a sort of balloon

indicators.note: In says the books go inside the shock

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Someone stunned by literature sees a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-air balloon rises on heated air, so the phrase names one kind of balloon.

clue.text: Old round locker found in intact caves

indicators.note: found in says the pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: whole means intact, undamaged
O is round in shape
a key locks things, so is a locker

explanation.surface: An ancient circular cabinet is discovered within undisturbed caverns.
explanation.walkthrough: Wookey Hole is a set of show caves in Somerset, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wookey Hole is a named system of limestone caverns, so it is an example of caves.

clue.text: Key issue before sorcerer

indicators.note: before places the issue piece ahead of the key

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, comes out as an issue
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An important matter comes up ahead of the wizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key issue' reads as a phrase meaning a vital matter, but the words split: Key is E, issue is MAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A mage is an old or literary word for a magician or wise wizard.

clue.text: See 3
Surprises an IRA commander returning some instruments

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone catches an IRA commander off guard as he comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks SANIRACO from 'Surprises an IRA commander'; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocarinas are small egg-shaped wind instruments, examples of the general term.

clue.text: Invoice alien for accommodation

parts.note: a bill is an invoice
ET is the film extraterrestrial, a stock alien

explanation.surface: A hotel bill handed to a foreigner for a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging, especially for soldiers in a private house, a kind of accommodation.

clue.text: In due course, appearance of embarrassment drops down to irritation

parts.note: so as an adverb can mean then, in due course

indicators.note: drops says the letter is let fall out of the word

parts.note: redness of the face shows embarrassment

explanation.surface: Eventually a flushed face fades and gives way to annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' takes the D (down) out of REDNESS, leaving RENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soreness is a painful, inflamed state, so it can stand for irritation of the skin or body.

clue.text: Moroccan resort oddly grand in song

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the song word

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of grand

explanation.surface: A North African holiday town features in a grand song.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a beach resort on Morocco's Atlantic coast, a specific example of the definition.
